'''Frank Carter Duckworth''' [[Order of the British Empire|MBE]] (26 December 1939 – 21 June 2024) was an English [[statistician]] who co-developed the [[Duckworth–Lewis method]] of resetting targets in [[limited overs cricket]] matches interrupted by weather or other circumstances.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/frank-duckworth-co-inventor-of-dls-method-dies-at-the-age-of-84-1440876 | title=Frank Duckworth, co-inventor of DLS method, dies at the age of 84 }}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=First Night: Duckworth–Lewis: The odd couple getting even with the weather|journal=[[The Independent]]|date=16 May 1999| url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/first-night-duckworthlewis-the-odd-couple-getting-even-with--the-weather-1093982.html | location=London | first=Andrew | last=Longmore | accessdate=2 May 2010}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=How two statisticians became stars|journal=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/02/18/sports/18iht-cricket_ed3__6.html|date=18 February 2003 |  first=Huw | last=Richards | accessdate=2 May 2010}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Duckworth was born on 26 December 1939 in [[Lytham St Annes]], [[Lancashire]].<ref name="ESPNcricinfo&nbsp;— Frank Duckworth&nbsp;— England">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/england/content/player/462809.html|title=Frank Duckworth&nbsp;— England|work=[[Cricinfo]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|accessdate=31 December 2011}}</ref> He attended King Edward VII School, Lytham, now part of [[King Edward VII and Queen Mary School]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.longridgenews.co.uk/news/tony-bowled-over-by-mbe-honour-1-2160953 |title=Tony bowled over by MBE honour |date=17 October 2010 |newspaper=Longridge and Ribble Valley News and Advertiser |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190821093753/https://www.longridgenews.co.uk/news/tony-bowled-over-by-mbe-honour-1-2160953 |archive-date=21 August 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref> then went on to study physics (BSc Hons 1961) and earned a PhD (1965) in metallurgy, both at the [[University of Liverpool]].<ref>{{citation |title=University of Liverpool Alumni Newsletter:Queen's Birthday Honours list 2010 |date=July 2010 |url=http://alumni.liv.ac.uk/NetCommunity/SSLPage.aspx?pid=969&frcrld=1 }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

==Career==
Prior to his retirement, he worked as a mathematical scientist for the English [[nuclear power]] industry.<ref>[http://billboard.anu.edu.au/event_view.asp?id=37384&printerfriendly=true The D/L Method in One-day Cricket: Twelve years on] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090709211102/http://billboard.anu.edu.au/event_view.asp?id=37384&printerfriendly=true |date=2009-07-09 }}. Announcement for talk by Duckworth at the [[Australian National University]], 20 February  2009</ref> He was a consultant statistician to the [[International Cricket Council]],<ref>{{citation|title=Duckworth to review D/L method, slams Indian rival |url=http://sports.in.msn.com/t20wc2009/article.aspx?cp-documentid=3042371 |publisher=[[MSN]] |date=17 June 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090619191537/http://sports.in.msn.com/t20wc2009/article.aspx?cp-documentid=3042371 |archivedate=June 19, 2009 }}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Duckworth, Lewis to attend World Cup Forum in Antigua |journal=Jamaica Observer |date=3 December 2005 |url=http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/sports/html/20051202T220000-0500_93799_OBS_DUCKWORTH__LEWIS_TO_ATTEND_WORLD_CUP_FORUM_IN_ANTIGUA.asp |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090709195106/http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/sports/html/20051202T220000-0500_93799_OBS_DUCKWORTH__LEWIS_TO_ATTEND_WORLD_CUP_FORUM_IN_ANTIGUA.asp |archivedate=July 9, 2009 }}.</ref> and the editor of the [[Royal Statistical Society]]'s monthly news magazine, ''RSS News'', until he retired from both these roles in 2014.<ref>[http://www.rss.org.uk/main.asp?page=1710 RSS News Editorial Team] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081223161124/http://www.rss.org.uk/main.asp?page=1710 |date=2008-12-23 }}, Royal Statistical Society.</ref> He also served on the editorial board of ''[[Significance (magazine)|Significance]]'' before stepping down in 2010. In 2004 he delivered the Royal Statistical Society Schools Lecture, entitled ''Lies and Statistics''.<ref>[http://www.rss.org.uk/main.asp?page=1918 RSS Schools Lecture (Guy Lecture)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090712020952/http://www.rss.org.uk/main.asp?page=1918 |date=2009-07-12 }} and [http://www.rss.org.uk/main.asp?page=2179 Past RSS Schools Lectures] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090712020956/http://www.rss.org.uk/main.asp?page=2179 |date=2009-07-12 }}, Royal Statistical Society</ref>

In 1962, Duckworth was a tenant of [[John Lennon]]'s aunt.<ref>{{cite news| url= https://www.thetimes.com/sport/cricket/article/frank-duckworth-and-tony-lewis-the-men-who-let-it-be-right-when-it-rains-mjjm8qkb9pc| title= Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis, the men who let it be right when it rains|work=[[The Times]]|url-access=subscription | date=15 April 2011| access-date=24 August 2018}}</ref>

Duckworth is also known for developing a system of quantifying personal [[risk perception]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/1999/jul/16/johnezard|journal=[[The Guardian]]|title=Riskometer measures life's ups and downs|date=16 July 1999 | location=London | first=John | last=Ezard | accessdate=2 May 2010}}</ref> now known as the "Duckworth scale".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.espn.com/espnmag/story?id=3576125|title=Editor's blog|journal=[[ESPN Magazine]]|first=Gary|last=Belsky|date=8 September 2008}}</ref>

==Death==
Duckworth died of cancer on 21 June 2024, at the age of 84.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorary graduates, 2010 to 2019 |url=https://www.bath.ac.uk/corporate-information/honorary-graduates-2010-to-2019/ |access-date=2025-08-22 |website=www.bath.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Frank Duckworth obituary: inventor of cricket's Duckworth-Lewis method |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/cricket/article/frank-duckworth-obituary-death-6t0z05bqn |access-date=14 July 2024 |publisher=The Times |date=26 June 2024}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Duckworth was appointed [[Member of the Order of the British Empire]] (MBE) in the [[2010 Birthday Honours]] for services to the Royal Statistical Society and to Cricket.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=59446 |date=12 June 2010 |page=15 |supp=y }}</ref>  He was also the recipient of the Degree of Doctor of Science, honoris causa. from the [[University of Bath]] in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-25 |title=Man who helped revolutionise rain-hit cricket dies aged 84 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c999w55dd5xo |access-date=2025-08-22 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Frank Carter Duckworth MBE: oration |url=https://www.bath.ac.uk/corporate-information/dr-frank-carter-duckworth-mbe-oration/ |access-date=2025-08-22 |website=www.bath.ac.uk}}</ref>
